title: Prologue (lines 1–155)
focus: a king who promises to find the killer

teacherSummary.text: Thebes is dying of a plague. Suppliants and a Priest beg King Oedipus, who once saved the city from the Sphinx, to save it again. Creon returns from Delphi: Apollo says the city must drive out the killer of the former king, Laius. Oedipus vows to "make dark things clear" and calls the people together.

significance: The man who solves riddles sets out to solve one more, and every promise he makes will turn back on him. The audience knows the myth; the king does not. That gap is dramatic irony.
discussionQuestions: Is a leader responsible for problems he did not knowingly cause? Why or why not?

anchorPassages.note: The ship-of-state and blight catalogue establish the civic crisis that drives the plot.
anchorPassages.text:
For, as thou seest thyself, our ship of State,
Sore buffeted, can no more lift her head,
Foundered beneath a weltering surge of blood.
A blight is on our harvest in the ear,
A blight upon the grazing flocks and herds,
A blight on wives in travail; and withal
Armed with his blazing torch the God of Plague
Hath swooped upon our city emptying
The house of Cadmus, and the murky realm
Of Pluto is full fed with groans and tears.
Therefore, O King, here at thy hearth we sit,
I and these children; not as deeming thee
A new divinity, but the first of men;
First in the common accidents of life,
And first in visitations of the Gods.
Art thou not he who coming to the town
Of Cadmus freed us from the tax we paid
To the fell songstress? Nor hadst thou received
Prompting from us or been by others schooled;
No, by a god inspired (so all men deem,
And testify) didst thou renew our life.

anchorPassages.note: Delphi names blood-guilt as the city's sore and sets the investigation in motion.
anchorPassages.text:
Let me report then all the god declared.
King Phoebus bids us straitly extirpate
A fell pollution that infests the land,
And no more harbour an inveterate sore.
What expiation means he? What’s amiss?
Banishment, or the shedding blood for blood.
This stain of blood makes shipwreck of our state.
Whom can he mean, the miscreant thus denounced?
Before thou didst assume the helm of State,
The sovereign of this land was Laius.
I heard as much, but never saw the man.
He fell; and now the god’s command is plain:
Punish his takers-off, whoe’er they be.
Where are they? Where in the wide world to find
The far, faint traces of a bygone crime?
In this land, said the god; “who seeks shall find;
Who sits with folded hands or sleeps is blind.”

anchorPassages.note: Dramatic irony: he swears to purge a poison that is already his own.
anchorPassages.text:
Well, I will start afresh and once again
Make dark things clear. Right worthy the concern
Of Phoebus, worthy thine too, for the dead;
I also, as is meet, will lend my aid
To avenge this wrong to Thebes and to the god.
Not for some far-off kinsman, but myself,
Shall I expel this poison in the blood;
For whoso slew that king might have a mind
To strike me too with his assassin hand.
Therefore in righting him I serve myself.
Up, children, haste ye, quit these altar stairs,
Take hence your suppliant wands, go summon hither
The Theban commons. With the god’s good help
Success is sure; ’tis ruin if we fail. Exeunt Oedipus and Creon.
